run.question:
I'm connected to the ci-cd cluster. We got a P1 alert and need help finding the root cause.
Our cluster inventory is in the app-235-cluster-inventory index and deployment/change history
is in the app-235-change-history index. Please search these indices to investigate.
[
  {
    "annotations": {
      "description": "Online Devices count gradual decrease over 8 hours in [clientorg-alpha] [56%] for over 30m",
      "workload": "clientorg-alpha"
    },
    "fingerprint": "xx1234567890abcd",
    "labels": {
      "alertname": "onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease",
      "app": "lambda-dashboard-monitoring",
      "cluster": "us-prod-eks",
      "grafana_dashboard_name": "Production-Performance-Overview",
      "org": "clientorg-alpha",
      "severity": "critical",
      "slack_channel": "sre-alerts-channel"
    },
    "startsAt": "30 minutes ago",
    "status": "firing"
  }
]
The alert started right after a deployment. Can you check what's the root cause?

report.summary: The alert's own entities could not be located in any data source in this Run, and the queryable telemetry splits into two disconnected pictures. (1) The ci-cd deployment/change record: app-235-change-history shows only three changes inside the authorized window, all in namespace ci on cluster ci-cd — jenkins 2.426.2-lts->2.426.3-lts at 03:33:14Z, argocd-server v2.9.2->v2.9.3 at 04:33:14Z, and a gitlab-runner scale 2->3 at 07:33:14Z — and app-235-cluster-inventory reports all three workloads (gitlab-runner, jenkins, argocd-server) as status Running. Nothing in those indices names clientorg-alpha, us-prod-eks, lambda-dashboard-monitoring or onlineDevicesCount, and the connected cluster has no ci namespace (it has app-162, otel-demo and system namespaces). (2) The connected cluster's only failing workload is namespace app-162: deployments payments-service (1 replica) and signup-service (2 replicas) were created at 2026-11-22T09:32:52Z and both report Available=False / MinimumReplicasUnavailable. The payments-service pod's liveness probe fails with HTTP 503, the container was killed and restarted (exit code 137), and its log states exactly "STRIPE_API_KEY is set to invalid test key - service will fail" and "Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key"; the STRIPE_API_KEY env comes from secretKeyRef payments-secrets/stripe-api-key, and the secret's value could not be read. The two signup-service pods never became ready and log "Payments service check failed: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>", consistent with payments-service having no ready endpoints. The otel-demo namespace (all deployments 1/1 ready) and the node were checked and look healthy; flagd's demo.flagd.json has every fault flag at defaultVariant off. Because Prometheus and Jaeger returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for every query in this Run, no error-rate, latency or trace evidence exists, so neither the alerting metric nor the link between the P1 alert and the app-162 failure could be established; the invalid-secret-value conclusion is also partly unverified because Secrets cannot be read.

claims.text: app-235-change-history contains three change records inside the authorized window, all in namespace ci on cluster ci-cd: gitlab-runner change BUILD-5PW2K6 type scale "Scaled gitlab-runner from 2 to 3 replicas" at 2026-11-22T07:33:14Z; argocd-server change BUILD-3NR8Y1 type deployment v2.9.2->v2.9.3 at 2026-11-22T04:33:14Z; jenkins change BUILD-7X4Q9M type deployment 2.426.2-lts->2.426.3-lts at 2026-11-22T03:33:14Z. None of them starts within about 30 minutes of the alert's implied start (2026-11-22T09:03:26Z, derived from the payload's relative "30 minutes ago").

app-235-cluster-inventory records cluster ci-cd, namespace ci: gitlab-runner (gitlab/gitlab-runner:v16.7.0, 3 replicas, last_updated 2026-11-22T07:33:14Z), jenkins (jenkins/jenkins:2.426.3-lts, 1 replica, last_updated 2026-11-22T03:33:14Z) and argocd-server (quay.io/argoproj/argocd:v2.9.3, 2 replicas, last_updated 2026-11-22T03:33:14Z), each with status Running. No failing status is recorded for these workloads in this index.

The namespace list returned for the connected cluster is app-162, default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo; it contains no ci namespace (the cluster named in the change history) and no app-95 namespace.

Namespace app-162 has two deployments, both created 2026-11-22T09:32:52Z with image python:3.11-slim: payments-service (spec.replicas 1, unavailableReplicas 1) and signup-service (spec.replicas 2, unavailableReplicas 2). Both carry the condition Available=False with message "Deployment does not have minimum availability." / reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable, and neither has readyReplicas or availableReplicas set.

The payments-service Deployment injects its credential as env STRIPE_API_KEY from secretKeyRef name payments-secrets key stripe-api-key, and mounts its application code from a volume whose secretName is payments-secrets; the signup-service Deployment sets env PAYMENTS_SERVICE_URL=http://payments-service:8080 and mounts app code from secretName signup-secrets. The values inside these Secrets cannot be read.

Events in namespace app-162 show Deployment payments-service ScalingReplicaSet "from 0 to 1" and Deployment signup-service "from 0 to 2" at 2026-11-22T09:32:52Z, the matching ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate events, pod Started events at 09:32:53Z, and then Warning event reason Unhealthy on pod payments-service-6d94c44fdc-zfk67 at 2026-11-22T09:33:23Z: "Liveness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503" (count 3) followed by Normal event Killing: "Container payments-service failed liveness probe, will be restarted".

Pod payments-service-6d94c44fdc-zfk67 has condition Ready=False / ContainersNotReady ("containers with unready status: [payments-service]"), restartCount 1, and container lastState.terminated with exitCode 137, reason Error, startedAt 2026-11-22T09:32:53Z, finishedAt 2026-11-22T09:33:53Z; the container is running again since 09:33:53Z and still not ready. Both signup-service pods (signup-service-7c89545dc9-rmrqm, -sc25s) are also Ready=False / ContainersNotReady with restartCount 0.

payments-service container log lines (09:32:55Z-09:33:23Z) read: "ERROR - STRIPE_API_KEY is set to invalid test key - service will fail", then repeated "ERROR - Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key", with probe requests logged as "GET /health HTTP/1.1" 503 and "GET /ready HTTP/1.1" 503 every few seconds. The error text states the Stripe API key itself is invalid.

signup-service container logs (09:32:58Z-09:33:23Z) repeat "ERROR - Payments service check failed: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>" with "GET /ready HTTP/1.1" 503 at the same timestamps, so signup-service readiness fails on its calls to payments-service.

Endpoint objects confirm the two app-162 Services have no ready backends: endpoints payments-service has no addresses and only notReadyAddresses 10.244.0.39; endpoints signup-service has no addresses and only notReadyAddresses 10.244.0.37 and 10.244.0.38. Every otel-demo endpoint listed (ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, flagd, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, load-generator, otel-collector, payment, product-catalog, quote, recommendation, shipping, valkey-cart, jaeger, prometheus, kube-state-metrics) has a ready address.

All 22 otel-demo application deployments returned by the deployments query report READY 1 and AVAIL 1 (ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, flagd, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, jaeger, kube-state-metrics, load-generator, otel-collector, payment, product-catalog, prometheus, prometheus-readonly-proxy, quote, recommendation, shipping, valkey-cart), and every otel-demo pod in the pod listing has container ready=true.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config key demo.flagd.json defines the fault flags productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad, and every one of them has defaultVariant "off" (state ENABLED).
The single node opspilot-m1-control-plane reports Ready=True with MemoryPressure=False, DiskPressure=False and PIDPressure=False ("kubelet is posting ready status").

An events query also recorded a Warning event reason FailedToCreateEndpoint at 2026-11-22T09:21:00Z for involvedObject kind Endpoints name orca: "Failed to create endpoint for service app-95/orca: endpoints \"orca\" already exists", and a second one at 09:32:52Z for service app-162/signup-service ("endpoints \"signup-service\" already exists"). No app-95 namespace object exists in the namespace list, so the orca object could not be read.

The fault that keeps payments-service from becoming ready is an invalid Stripe API key stored in Secret app-162/payments-secrets under key stripe-api-key: that Secret is the only source of the container's STRIPE_API_KEY env, and the container log states the key it received is an invalid test key and that health checks fail for that reason. The Secret's contents are unreadable, so the stored value itself was not verified and it cannot be excluded that the same invalid value is hard-coded elsewhere.

The signup-service readiness failures are a downstream consequence of payments-service rather than an independent fault: signup-service's readiness probe calls http://payments-service:8080 and logs connection refused, while the payments-service Service has no ready endpoints because its only pod never passes readiness — consistent with kube-proxy rejecting connections to a ClusterIP with no ready backends.

Whether the app-162 failure is the same incident as the P1 alert is unresolved: the alert names cluster us-prod-eks, workload clientorg-alpha and app lambda-dashboard-monitoring, none of which appears in the ci-cd inventory, the change history, the connected cluster's objects, or (per the empty index search) the Elasticsearch documents; and the app-162 deployments at 09:32:52Z are younger than the alert's implied ~09:03Z start, so they cannot have caused it if that timing is accurate.

Rejected as the cause: an enabled flagd fault-injection flag in otel-demo. The demo.flagd.json read in this Run shows every fault flag (including paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable) at defaultVariant "off", and the payment deployment and its pod are ready, so no observed otel-demo fault is attributable to flagd.

Rejected as the trigger: the three ci-cd changes recorded inside the window (jenkins 2.426.3-lts at 03:33:14Z, argocd-server v2.9.3 at 04:33:14Z, gitlab-runner scale 2->3 at 07:33:14Z). None of them occurred right before the alert's implied ~09:03:26Z start, the inventory records all three workloads as Running, and no evidence ties any of them to the app-162 payments-service failure or to a device-count metric.

Cluster-level infrastructure pressure is not supported as a cause for the app-162 readiness failures: the only node reports Ready=True with no memory, disk or PID pressure, and both failing deployments were created minutes before observation with resources requests cpu 100m / memory 128Mi and limits cpu 200m / memory 256Mi, so the liveness failure is not explained by node pressure.

The otel-demo namespace was checked and shows no failing workload: all its application deployments are 1/1 ready, all its pods have ready=true, and all its Service endpoints have ready addresses; its pods' restarts predate the window. That is a checked-and-healthy finding for otel-demo, not evidence about the alerting workload.

Restore access to the payments-service credential: read Secret app-162/payments-secrets key stripe-api-key through an authorized secret-reading path (this Run cannot read Secrets), replace the invalid test Stripe key with a valid one, and restart/roll the payments-service Deployment so readiness and the payments-service endpoints recover; signup-service readiness should then clear without its own change.

Find who created the app-162 payments-service and signup-service Deployments at 2026-11-22T09:32:52Z (there is no app-235-change-history record for them) and correct the release process that shipped an invalid Stripe test key into the payments-secrets credential.

To resolve the P1 alert itself, obtain evidence from cluster us-prod-eks and workload clientorg-alpha / app lambda-dashboard-monitoring (that cluster's inventory, change history and the onlineDevicesCount series), and re-enable Prometheus and Jaeger access so error-rate and latency signals can be read; none of those entities was reachable from this Run's authorized targets.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable for the whole Run: execute_prometheus_instant_query at 2026-11-22T09:20:00Z and 09:34:08Z, metrics_range_query (08:53-09:33Z and 08:30-09:33Z) and get_label_values all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, and one metrics_range_query was refused as INVALID_PARAMS before sending. Therefore no error-rate, throughput or latency reading exists in this Run, and the alerting signal onlineDevicesCount (or any Prometheus alerting rule for onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease) could not be evaluated or baselined.

Jaeger was unreachable as well (traces_list_services, traces_search and traces_search_by_tags all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no span, status-code or trace-chain evidence exists; the effect of the app-162 failure on callers and the otel-demo request paths are unobserved.

The alert's entities are not present in the queryable data: an Elasticsearch query_string search over app-235-* for clientorg/us-prod/lambda-dashboard/onlineDevices/payments/signup returned no documents (and one matched index, app-235-change-history, does not map last_updated so it could not match that filter), and no Kubernetes object carries those names. That is 'not found', not proof of absence.

Secret values could not be read: the content of Secret app-162/payments-secrets (key stripe-api-key) and signup-secrets is unverified, so the exact invalid value and whether it is the sole source of STRIPE_API_KEY remain unconfirmed; the invalid-key statement rests on the application's own log line.

3 of the 6 documents in app-235-cluster-inventory and 1 of the 4 documents in app-235-change-history fall outside the authorized window (last_updated/timestamp before 2026-11-21T09:33:26Z) and were dropped by the time filter, so those records are unknown.

No change-history record exists inside the window for the app-162 payments-service / signup-service deployments created at 2026-11-22T09:32:52Z, and 3 cluster events were dropped for lying outside the authorized window; what change process created those Deployments is unverified.

The previous instance logs of pod payments-service-6d94c44fdc-zfk67 are unavailable ("previous terminated container not found") and 5 log lines after the window were dropped, so the pre-restart instance's log is unknown.

Kubernetes resourcequotas and networkpolicies queries returned no_data; an empty result cannot be used to state that none exist or that they are not involved, so quota- and policy-based causes are unchecked rather than excluded.

The alert's start time is only given relatively ("30 minutes ago"); the ~09:03:26Z estimate used here is derived from the run window, so the exact deviation point of the alerting signal and whether the 09:32:52Z app-162 deployment preceded or followed it is unverified.
The Endpoints/orca event names service app-95/orca, but no app-95 namespace or object is readable, so that object and its relation (if any) to this incident remain a gap.
next_steps: Read Secret app-162/payments-secrets key stripe-api-key via an authorized path, correct the invalid Stripe key, and roll the payments-service Deployment; then verify readiness of payments-service and signup-service pods and that their Service endpoints become ready.

Query cluster us-prod-eks for the alerting workload clientorg-alpha / app lambda-dashboard-monitoring (deployment and change records plus the onlineDevicesCount series) to link or separate the alert from the app-162 failure.
Restore Prometheus/Jaeger connectivity and evaluate the onlineDevicesCount alerting rule and per-service error-rate and latency series across the 8-hour decline window with a comparable baseline.
Identify the apply path that created the app-162 Deployments at 2026-11-22T09:32:52Z and add those releases to app-235-change-history, since none was recorded.
Inspect resourcequotas and networkpolicies with a source that can list them, since the current queries returned no_data.
